title: sqlc: SQL that becomes typed Go code

videos.script: Lesson 6 wrote the SQL and the Go that reads it, and kept the two in step by hand. Lesson 7 let an ORM write the SQL, out of sight. {{idea}} sqlc takes the third way. You write the SQL. A program writes the Go. {{install}} It needs a C compiler to build, because it uses PostgreSQL's own parser. So gcc arrives in this lesson. {{generate}} Then four queries, a short configuration, and one command. Out come a hundred and forty-six lines of typed Go you can read. {{bug}} boxoffice's store switches to it, and one request finds a real bug. Event four billion and something answers as event one. {{catch}} Next, what sqlc catches. A typo in a column name slips through, until sqlc is allowed to ask the database. {{filters}} And the one place sqlc gets awkward: a search where every filter is optional.
